messages:
emily_cs: Escalation from customer: batch rerank calls keep failing for multi-query jobs. They see 400 / candidate_count_mismatch or scores shifted by one for some queries. Happens intermittently when they upload from CSV -> our CSV-to-json helper. Example they pasted:

emily_cs: curl example they sent:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank/batch \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"queries": ["q1","q2","q3"], "candidates": [["a","b"],["c"],["d","e","f"]] }'
```

emily_cs: Server response they get sporadically:
```
{"error":"candidate_index_out_of_range","message":"candidate_count_mismatch: expected 2 candidates for query 0"}
```

emily_cs: Customer notes workaround: flattening candidates + sending per-query counts in a custom header seems to sometimes work, but not reliably. Asking for root cause and repro steps. :eyes:

sam_engineer: Can you paste the raw payload (exact bytes) and the header set? CSV -> JSON helpers often drop empty arrays or stringify counts differently. Also which client version?

support-bot: TICKET-3621 created (P2) for customer escalation.

jordank: Pasted server log snippet we saw for one repro run:
```
ERROR rerank.batch (handler.go:214) - candidate_count_mismatch: len(flat_candidates)=6 sum(per_query_counts)=5
stack: rerank/mapper.go:88 -> rerank/handler.go:202
payload_id=abc123 customer_id=456
```

jordank: Note: sums not matching, server rejected with 400. No helpful line-level mapping in the log (we'll add).

liz_h: Did this start after the client 1.2.0 release? There was a change around how CSV helper emits empty candidate slots. Might be related. @sam_engineer any idea?

sam_engineer: Looking. Two likely suspects: (1) client puts per-query counts in a header that our parser expects as comma-separated ints but some clients send JSON array string, and our header parser splits on "," only. (2) CSV helper sometimes turns empty columns into missing array entries which reduces sum.

sam_engineer: Quick repro I just ran (python requests):
```
payload = {
  "queries": ["q1", "q2"],
  "candidates": ["a","b","c"]  # client flattened everything
}
# header: X-PerQuery-Counts: "[2,1]"  <- some client libs send this quoted
r = requests.post(URL, json=payload, headers={"X-PerQuery-Counts":"[2,1]"})
print(r.status_code, r.text)
```

sam_engineer: When header is a quoted JSON array our header parser currently does str.split(',') on the header value which yields ['[2','1]'] -> parse error or wrong counts. That leads to sum mismatch.

ashley_rnd: I reproduced with CSV->json helper. The helper emits an empty candidate list for a query as an empty cell, and our CSV importer turns that into completely missing entry in flat list instead of an explicit empty array. So two independent failure modes: quoted header and CSV empty->drop.

ashley_rnd: Root cause is a brittle parsing codepath introduced in parser v0.9.4: header parsing uses strings.Split(header, ",") and then Atoi on each token without trimming brackets/quotes. Also CSV importer path used `filter(len>0)` which removed placeholders.

ashley_rnd: Proposed fixes: (a) robust header parse: accept JSON arrays and plain csv strings, trim [] and quotes; (b) ensure CSV importer keeps empty candidate slots as explicit empty arrays; (c) emit detailed mapping logs when sum mismatch occurs so support can show customer mapping. I'll open a PR.

sam_engineer: Thanks. Can you add a minimal server-side fallback: if sum(per_query_counts) != len(flat_candidates) then attempt to parse header as JSON array and as whitespace-trimmed CSV before rejecting. Also log the raw header + parsed tokens to help debugging.

ashley_rnd: Will do. Pushed draft fix to branch fix/rerank-header-parse and added unit tests for inputs: '2,1', '[2,1]', '"[2,1]"', '2, 1', and header missing. Tests cover empty candidate slots too.

liz_h: Any ETA for hotfix? Customer is P2 and hitting production.

sam_engineer: I can ship a hotfix to staging today, prod tomorrow (1.2.3) if QA green. Workaround for customer: send per_query_counts in request body (field name `per_query_counts`) instead of header OR ensure header is plain CSV with no brackets (e.g., `2,1,3`). Please pass that to them.

support-bot: Customer notified of workaround; assigned to sam_engineer for rollout.

emily_cs: Customer applied body workaround and confirmed no more errors for 6 runs in a row. :thumbsup: They will hold off on large batches until our fix deploys.

ashley_rnd: Merged fix to main after review; will cut 1.2.3 tomorrow morning. Added mapping logs for mismatch cases and an alert when empty-candidate-drop is detected.

emily_cs: Closing loop with customer, marking TICKET-3621 as awaiting deployment verification. Thanks all.
